subject: design-technology
title: Test, Evaluate, Iterate
welcome_lead: Specifications, criteria, and the feedback loop.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: testing, evaluation, and iterative refinement.

concepts.def: Measurable list of requirements a design must meet.
Standards used to judge a prototype against the brief.
Observing real users perform tasks with a prototype.
Comparing two design variants on a metric.

walkthroughs.body_html: A-Level designers use ACCESS-FM to write specifications: Aesthetics, Cost, Customer, Environment, Size, Safety, Function, Materials. Every spec point should be measurable.
Combine usability testing (real users), heuristic evaluation (expert), A/B testing (quantitative comparison) and analytic methods (Fitts' law, cognitive walkthrough) for thorough evaluation.
Each iteration logs what changed, why, and what was learned. Examiners reward visible iteration evidence — not a single 'perfect' solution but a documented trail of refinement.
